Commentary.Commentary: So that ends a pretty one-sided game in Port Elizabeth. One expected Sri Lanka to carry on from the momentum gained in the T20Is but South Africa were just too strong for them today, ironically on a pitch which suited the tourists more. The series now moves to Durban where the second ODI will be played under lights. Can the Lankans come back and level the series? Join us on Wednesday, 1st February, 2017 at 1330 local (1130 GMT). Adios! Take Care!

Man of the Match, Imran Tahir is very happy with the way he bowled today. Calls it a pleasing day for him and the team. Believes that he always wants to contribute, not take anything for granted. Playing every game for South Africa is an honour and he tries to give more than 200 percent. Informs that today is his wedding anniversary and his wife wanted him to take five wickets.  He is happy to have taken three and getting the Man of the Match. Calls it tough bowling against the wind as it made it easier for the batsmen. Mentions that he just wanted to bowl to his field, somehow he managed to get the wickets using his variations. Opines that the most pleasing thing is that he did not go away from his plans. Credits the fast bowlers for starting well. Calls it an honor to do well for South Africa. Ends up saying that the celebrations are taking a lot of energy but it just shows how much it means to him and it is what keeps him going.

Victorious South African skipper, AB de Villiers,  says that it was a good performance. The wicket was slow and low, which is actually suited to Sri Lanka but his team adjusted well. Credits the bowlers for setting up the win. Praises his new-ball bowlers for bowling with a lot of intensity and later, Imran Tahir, who controlled the game in the middle overs. On his captaincy on a windy day, he says that he felt that it was a bit windy but he used the experience he had gained while playing a game in Hambantota. Says that he has plenty of experience in the tank for ideas. On the field, he has Hashim Amla and Faf du Plessis. Feels that 180 was way below par. Had expected 250 to be difficult to chase down. Praises his openers for seeing off bowlers whom the team has not played much. Stresses that South Africa are up for it in the ODI series and expects Sri Lanka to come back hard in the second ODI, especially after they fared so well in the T20Is.

Sri Lanka skipper, Upul Tharanga starts off admitting that they did not begin well. Chandimal and Mendis had a partnership but they did not manage to come back after that start. Calls it a slow wicket and credits South African bowlers for hitting the right areas. Mentions that his spinners can come into the game if they have a score on board but opines that his spinners could not control the flow. Admits that they have a lot of areas to improve going ahead. Ends by saying that they will sit together and have a chat about the coming days.

It was the bowlers who set the game up for the hosts when they won the toss and inserted Sri Lanka. Wayne Parnell took out the Lankan openers early but Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal threatened to get the visitors back in the game. It was Imran Tahir, who broke the back of the innings with a tight spell of 3/26. It was a near perfect game for the hosts that gave them the 1-0 lead in the five-match ODI series.

That's as clinical as it gets from South Africa! Chasing a score of 182, the South Africa openers got them off to good start with a 71-run stand. Sri Lankan bowlers could not use the new balls as they would have liked and the spinners lacked the bite and guile of Tahir to make an impact. Amla missed out on a big score, getting out on 57. Faf du Plessis then hit a fine fifty and he along with AB de Villiers completed the formalities as South Africa romped home with as many as 15.4 overs to spare with eight wickets in hand.

FOUR! There is the winning shot! Full and outside off, Faf gently opens the face of the bat and guides it past short third man for a boundary! A comprehensive 8-wicket win for the hosts with 94 balls to spare!
24th ODI fifty for Faf du Plessis!
Scores are level! Half century for the Test skipper as well. A good knock in an easy run chase. Landed outside off, worked through square leg for a couple.
Could be the final over of the match...
Landed outside off, de Villiers looks to play the reverse sweep but misses.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Landed outside off, AB gently plays the reverse sweep and gets it through third man. Lakshan Sandakan gets across from short third man but does not dive, nor does he slide, just tries to stop it with both hands and misses. The ball goes through to the fence. AB moves to 30 from 26 balls with his third boundary.
Landed outside off, tucked through square leg for one.
Full and outside off, worked through square leg for a run.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single. 9 more needed from 101 balls now.
FOUR! HANDSOME! Full and outside off, de Villiers stays leg side of the ball and drives it through the covers for a boundary! The stand moves to 41 from 43 balls.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Goes back and gently nudges it through fine leg. A fielder runs to his right from fine leg and slides near the boundary to stop the ball. Three runs taken.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Can't even call it the last throw of the dice, Kusal Mendis called on for a bowl.
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for one more. Just 19 more needed from 108 balls.
Outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, FdP gets down and paddles it fine for a single. The stand moves to 30 from 35 balls.
Now he stays back and just pushes his bat ahead, but the ball just comes in and hits the pad.
Full and outside off, Faf lunges to push it towards the off side but gets a thick inside edge towards mid-wicket instead.
Landed outside off, spins in, bounces extra, du Plessis defends calmly.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Comes down the track and works it through square leg for a brace.
Landed outside off, AB gets back and across and punches it towards the bowler.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
FOUR! Full and around off, de Villiers gets down and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary!
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
There is a long on in place now.
Landed outside off, another reverse sweep played but straight to short third man.
Full and outside off, de Villiers looks to play the reverse sweep but mistimes it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pushes this down to long on for a single. 29 more needed from 123 balls.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, Faf gets down and gently paddles it fine for a couple. The stand moves to 21 from 20 balls.
SIX! BANG! Dropped short outside off, de Villiers goes back and pulls it massively over mid-wicket! 150 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA! 11 from the over.
Full and wide outside off, driven towards widish extra cover for one.
Goes back and works it to long leg for a run.
Full and outside off, de Villiers gets down and paddles it fine for a couple.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full toss outside off, driven through long off for a single.
Jeffrey Vandersay returns for a bowl.
Punches down to long off for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, pushed straight to point.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, pushed down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a run.
Down the leg side, helped away for a single.
Landed outside off, whipped straight to short mid-wicket.
AB de Villiers comes out to bat.

OUT! Caught and bowled! Gunaratne gets Amla. Nothing on the ball, nothing in the shot and that is a no result, for South Africa. Gunaratne bowls this outside off, fuller in length, but takes pace off the ball. Amla looks to hit it straight back but does not bother to keep it down. The elevation is not that great either to get it over the bowler and Asela leaps to take the catch. Amla departs to a loose shot but he played a much, much better innings today. Just 51 MORE NEEDED from 145 balls.
Full and just outside off, Hashim defends it watchfully.
On middle and off, punched down to long on for a run. The stand moves to 60 from 74 balls.
Shorter in length outside off, punched down to long off for a single.
Landed outside off, Amla looks to run it down to third man but misses as he does not move his feet.
Asela Gunaratne called into the attack for a bowl.

This is on middle now, FdP calmly flicks it through square leg. It is straight to the fielder but still they run two on what is considered to be a small ground. That might have been three or more at the MCG.  Faf moves to 30 from 43 balls.
Slightly slower outside off, tossing it up a little, Faf delays his cover drive a touch but still misses.
Full and outside off, du Plessis lunges and pushes the ball with an open bat-face towards point.
The length is not that different from the previous one but still HA goes back and works it through square leg for a single.
Fullish this time, Hashim looks to flick and almost gets a leading edge back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, spinning in, Amla goes back and punches towards cover.
FOUR! Second boundary of the over. Full and wide outside off, du Plessis reaches out and drives it behind point for a boundary! 11 from the over.
Outside off, punched straight to point.
Short and outside off, punched in front of cover for a run.
50-run stand up between Faf and Amla!
Banged in short, pulled through square leg for a run.

FOUR! GORGEOUS! Full and outside off, du Plessis drives this straight back past the bowler. Mid on and mid off are inside the circle and can only go to the ropes to fetch the ball back. Moves to 23 from 37 balls with his third boundary.
A short ball outside off, pulled through square leg for a single.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.

Oohhh... landed around middle, Faf goes back and pushes it in an awkward manner towards mid-wicket. Chandimal appeals for LBW and Sandakan joins him. The umpire says no. Sandakan scratches his head and looks towards Tharanga who just turns his back on him. Chandimal looks flummoxed. Perhaps when he looks at the replays later he will understand. That was off the bat and only of the bat. Nothing else.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a run.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Landed outside off, pretty wide, du Plessis gets down on a knee and looks to punch but misses.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for one.
Outside off, steered to third man for a run.
Excellent yorker outside off, Amla digs it back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, punched through sweeper cover for a single. The stand moves to 40 from 50 balls.
A bouncer outside off, Faf looks to pull but lets it through.
Full toss on middle, du Plessis flicks it towards mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right and gets a hand to it.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side.
Full and outside off, driven straight down the ground.
Outside off, steered behind point for one more.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a run.
Shorter in length around off, du Plessis goes back and punches it through the covers. There is a diving effort by the fielder but still the single is taken.
Full and around middle and off, watchfully defended.
Change of ends for Lakshan Sandakan.
On middle and off, FdP walks down the track and pushes this towards mid on for a quick one.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Faf misses his flick.
Full and outside off, du Plessis plays a flashy drive but misses.
Full and outside off, driven straight back. Lakmal gets down in his follow-through.
31st ODI fifty for Hashim Amla!

Gets the gap this time and reaches his half century. A controlled innings, much like the Amla we know, unlike the one we have been seeing of late. A length ball outside off, Amla gets across and punches this in front of point for a single.
Similar ball, similar shot, same result. Cannot find the gap.
On a good length outside off, Amla taps this towards point.
Suranga Lakmal is called back on for a bowl. The wind has picked up again. We are just an over from having 20 overs which assures us of a winner. Just in case, the heavens open up.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Dropped short, pulled away for one more.
Outside off, played straight to point.

FOUR! FLAMBOYANT! Full and wide outside off, du Plessis reaches out and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA and they barely look in trouble at all. Faf moves to 12 from 19 balls with his second boundary. The stand moves to 31 from 32 deliveries.
Full on middle, worked through square leg for a single.

SAFE. Nothing in it actually. Flighted around off, Amla prods but is beaten as the ball spins away. Chandimal takes the bails off in a flash and appeals for a stumping as Amla just about lifts his foot in the air a bit. It is referred upstairs but replays show that Amla is safe.
A stumping appeal against Amla has been referred upstairs. Looked not out to the naked eye.
FOUR! Fine shot. Full and wide outside off, du Plessis leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 14 from the over.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, run down behind point for a single. 89 more needed from 194 balls.

FIVE PENALTY RUNS! Bonus for South Africa. Pitched outside leg, Amla shuffles across to flick but misses. Dinesh Chandimal is blinded and misses the ball as it spins away from him. Unfortunately for Sri Lanka, the ball hits the helmet kept behind and that is five extra runs to the batting team. The stand moves to 20 from 26 balls.
A full toss outside off, driven straight to cover.
FOUR! Full and outside leg, Amla gets down and sweeps it very fine, through fine leg for a boundary.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads towards square leg.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and well outside off, Faf lunges to defend but misses and is hit on the pads again. Another LBW appeal but the impact was outside off.
Outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
An LBW appeal but inside edge was involved. Full and outside off, du Plessis lunges to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Short and outside off, punched down to long on for a single. 99 more needed from 203 balls now.
Drinks.
Flatter on middle, kept out by du Plessis watchfully.
Pushes this one to covers from his crease.

Huge shout for an lbw but not given! Sandakan bowls it on the stumps, Faf is beaten on his back foot as the ball spins away sharply and squares him up. The ball hits Faf on the back pad and the players go up long and hard for an lbw appeal but the umpire stays put. Tharanga has a chat with the bowler about the review but is taking his time. By the time he is convinced and opts for the review, the umpire tells him the time is up. Replays show it might still be a good decision that he was timed out and he could not go for the review as it looked to be pitching outside leg.
Too full on the pads, Amla clips it through mid on for a single.
Lands it on middle, Amla comes forward and pushes it towards covers from his crease.
Too full on middle, du Plessis nudges it down to long on for a single.
FOUR! In the gap! Floats it outside off, Amla goes for the big shot over covers. It flies past the backward point fielder and runs into the third man fence for a boundary.
Amla comes forward and defends it towards extra cover.
Fires it outside off, Amla stays back and defends it watchfully.
Lands it outside off, Faf punches it through covers for a single.
Fires it on the pads, Amla works it through backward square leg for a single.
Vandersay has a chat with the captain.
Too full on middle, du Plessis pushes it through mid off for a single.
Faf pushes it through for a single through covers.
WIDE! Faf shuffles across to clip it through but fails to clip it through. It was down the leg side and hence given a wide.
Bowls it a touch short, du Plessis goes back to cut it but the ball goes off the inside edge past the stumps.
Bowls the other one outside off, Faf plays for the turn and is beaten.
Fuller on off, du Plessis pushes it back down the wicket. the bowler goes to his left and stops the ball.
Stays back and defends it watchfully.
Faf du Plessis walks in to bat. There is a slip and short leg in place.

OUT! Sandakan strikes! Bowls this wider outside off, de Kock looks to go aerial but does not get the placement right and finds the fielder at extra cover. That is superbly held by the debutant, Weerakkody. End of a vital stand for SA. De Kock is not happy as he walks off the field.
Amla comes forward and defends it watchfully.
FOUR! Full toss from Vandersay, Amla makes most of it by smashing it wide of the mid on fielder for a boundary. Big over this for SA!
FOUR! Amla is toying with the field now! Stays back to this shorter one and cuts it through cover-point for a boundary. Superb shot, that!
Leaves this quicker one outside off.

SIX! Amla goes BOOM! Floats it outside off, Amla winds up for the big shot, gets under it and clobbers it straight down the ground for a maximum. He went after the width there which allowed him to free his arms.
Bowls it around off, Amla punches it back to the bowler off his back foot.
FOUR! Poor ball and punished! Shorter outside off, de Kock makes him pay with a fierce cut through backward point for a boundary. Superb over for the home side.
Lands it outside leg, Amla turns it through square leg for a single.
Shorter outside off, Amla cuts it towards point but to the fielder.
Long off drops back for Amla.
Lands it on off,  de Kock pushes it towards covers for a single.
Lands it on off, de Kock gets an inside edge as he aims to defend it coming forward.
FOUR! Wonderful shot! Floats it on off, de Kock comes forward and just pushes it into the gap at covers. The timing is too good and de Kock gets a boundary. Superb placement! 50 up for SA!
Another change, Lakshan Sandakan comes on for a bowl. He's called on now that he can have protection in the deep.
A touch quicker outside off, Amla comes forward and pushes it towards the off side.
Drops it short outside off, de Kock cuts it through covers for a single.
Lands it outside off, keeps a touch low, Amla counters the low bounce well and punches it through covers for a single.
Quicker one outside off from Vandersay, Amla lets it go.
Floats it on off, Amla does not pick it at first but gets his bat down in time to keep it out.
Bowls it on the pads, Amla stays back and works it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Another change, Jeffrey Vandersay brought into the attack by Tharanga.
The umpire signals the start of the second Powerplay. Four players are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
Landed outside off, Amla leans forward and clips it through mid-wicket for a run. End of a good Powerplay for South Africa.
de Kock slinks down, eases a single to long off.
Landed outside off, Amla comes a touch and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
de Kock covers the line and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Edged! Slight turn from de Silva on a length ball outside off, de Kock gets an edge towards point but no runs taken.
Worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Another quick single by Amla towards mid on. The fielder missed his shy at the non-striker's end.

de Kock had given up! Landed outside off, de Kock comes across to work it through the on side but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards covers and Amla calls him through for a single. de Kock responds but Asela at covers is quick to it. He has a shy in one motion but misses. de Kock had given up hopes but luckily for him, the shy was wide of the stumps.
A drizzle has picked up again. Seems like yet another passing shower.
Fuller outside off, de Kock times his push towards covers.
Full outside off, Amla dabs it down to third man for a single.

FOUR! Gift from Nuwan! Low full toss around off, Amla does not miss out on the gift and lofts it just over mid on for a boundary. That was nicely picked and hit away despite coming off the bottom half of the bat.
Amla gets across a touch and defends it back down the wicket. He was looking to work it through the leg side but had to play straighter at the end.
Landed on off, Amla looks to work it through the on side but gets a leading edge for a single towards mid off.
On the stumps, de Kock leans into it and turns it towards mid-wicket for a brisk single.
Too full on middle, Amla clips it towards mid-wicket for a single.
de Kock comes down the wicket to go inside out but gets it off the inner half through mid on for a single.
The wind is too strong and the bails lite up by themselves. Slight hold up in play.
Shorter outside off, de Kock goes back to cut it but finds the fielder at backward point.
Floats it on the stumps, de Kock comes down and turns it towards mid on.
Time for spin! Dhananjaya de Silva to bowl now.
Angled on a shorter length, de Kock pulls it through square leg for a single.
Bowls it from outside off, Amla walks across and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter outside off, de Kock controls his pull shot through square leg for a single.
Bowls it on off, Amla looks to cover the inward movement and just about gets his bat down in time to get it through square leg for a single.
Length ball outside off, de Kock works it through square leg for a single.
Shorter outside off, de Kock goes for the pull shot despite not quite being in position to do so. Two runs taken as the ball goes in the deep at mid-wicket.
Outside off, de Kock gets across and turns it through mid-wicket for a single.
Good length outside off, Amla punches it towards point off his crease for a single.
Top ball! Hurls it on a length just around off, Amla stays in his crease and looks to play at it. The ball shapes away late and beats Amla all ends up.
It has gone a bit dark at the ground.
Angled on a length on off, de Kock taps it towards point for a single. There is a shy at the striker's end but misses.
FOUR! Edged! Outside off on a length, de Kock throws his bat at it. The ball goes off the edge down to third man for a boundary.
On a length outside off, de Kock defends it from his crease.
Length ball outside off, Amla punches it on the up towards covers from his crease.
On a length on off, Amla stays in his crease, opens his face of the bat and gets it towards point. Good change of pace there from Nuwan.
Shorter length outside off, Amla looks to pull it through but the ball bounces a touch more and beats the batsman.
Good length on off, de Kock gets across and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Bowls it outside off, de Kock comes across and defends it towards covers.
Square leg is in place now.
On a length on off, de Kock gets across and turns it towards mid on from his crease.
Length ball outside off, Amla chops it towards point from his crease.
Amla gets across and defends it towards mid on.
Outside off on a length, de Kock gets across and works it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Nicely bowled! Lakmal bowls it outside off, comes in a long way, de Kock looks to defend but is beaten by the inward movement on that one.
Fuller length outside off, de Kock strides forward and drives it to covers.
Goes round the wicket.

FOUR! Brilliant shot! Fuller outside off, de Kock gets across and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary. There was a fielder who dived to his right at mid-wicket but could not stop the ball. Nice shot, Quinton!
On a length on off, de Kock clips it wide of mid on and takes a quick single.
Length outside off, Amla slices it over backward point for a single. He actually wanted to play it a lot straighter.
Fuller outside off, Amla times his drive to mid off with a lunge.
On a length outside off, Amla this time waits for it and punches it through covers. Two fielders give it a chase and keep the ball in play. A couple of runs to Amla to get off the mark.
Outside off on a length, Amla flays it hard but to the fielder at point.
Fuller outside off, Amla covers the line and defends it watchfully.
Too full outside off, de Kock clips it towards mid on from his crease with a shuffle.
Pitched up outside off, de Kock looks to punch it through mid on but finds the fielder. The ball has not quite come onto the bat that well.
Fuller in length on off, de Kock turns it towards square leg from his place.
A touch short on off, de Kock places it towards point from his crease.
This time he connects with his drive but finds the fielder at mid off.

Did it carry? Nope! Fuller length outside off, de Kock comes down walking to drive it through mid on but gets an outside edge. The ball does not carry to Kusal Mendis at first slip who dives forward but cannot take the catch. Nice start for Lakmal!
Suranga Lakmal to bowl with the second new ball from the other end.
Angles it on a length around off, Amla gets across and pushes it towards mid on.
Pitched up outside off, Amla mistimes his drive towards covers.
Fuller outside off, left alone by Amla watchfully.
De Kock works one through square leg for a single to get off the mark.
Outside off, de Kock punches it down the ground towards mid off.
Starts off with a length ball but on the pads, de Kock looks to clip it but gets it off the pads to fine leg for a couple of leg byes.
Welcome back for the chase! The two South Africa openers Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock are out to bat. Sri Lanka begin with Nuwan Kulasekara! Here we go...
